Twenty-Four Seasons In:

LeBron James Still Treats The Tunnel Like A Runway

The Closet Style Desk5 min read
Monogram leather, head to toe color blocking, the full LeBron tunnel formula in one frame.

LeBron James is heading into his 24th season with a new team for the first time since 2018, a two year deal in Philadelphia he's called his "last decision." Everything else around him is in flux: new arena, new teammates, a new city learning his pregame walk. The walk itself hasn't changed at all. Whatever uniform he's about to put on, the outfit he wears to get there is still doing exactly what it's always done: saying something, on purpose, before he's said a word.

The Louis Vuitton Loyalty

Start with the obvious thread. James has been a Louis Vuitton ambassador since Pharrell Williams took over as the house's menswear creative director in 2023, and it shows in almost everything he wears backstage. The monogram biker jacket above is textbook: the leather goodyear-welted into a moto silhouette, the canvas covered edge to edge in LV's classic pattern, worn open over a plain sweatshirt so the jacket does all the talking.

The embroidered denim two-piece, LV logos and small figures worked into the fabric, styled with the house's own duffel.

The denim two-piece is the deeper cut. Louis Vuitton has released embroidered denim overshirts under the Pharrell era with tiny portrait motifs stitched throughout, a detail that reads as pure texture from a distance and reveals itself as actual artwork up close. Pairing it with the brand's own duffel instead of a generic bag is the kind of consistency that separates an ambassador from someone just wearing the clothes.

Price Watch
LV embroidered denim overshirts (this silhouette) start around $6,400
Based on Louis Vuitton's Spring-Summer menswear pricing for comparable embroidered denim pieces. BeyondStyle tracks resale and retail movement on pieces like this as they come in and out of stock.

The One Fit That Wasn't Trying

Not every walk is a campaign moment, though. Backstage at a Lakers home game, James kept it to a sheer crochet knit camp shirt, cropped grey trousers, and a pair of low profile sneakers. No monogram in sight. It's the outfit that proves the point better than the logo pieces do: he doesn't need the branding to look considered, he needs three pieces that actually fit and a reason to wear them together.

No logos, just proportion: a cropped knit shirt and tapered grey trouser, backstage at Crypto.com Arena.

Off Duty Still Means On Brand

Even the road game, lower key version of the fit stays consistent. A checkerboard denim jacket over a plain white tee, black trousers, white sneakers, and an LV belt buckle doing quiet work at the waist, finished with a camo print bucket hat that's the only genuinely playful piece in the whole rotation. It's the most "getting off a bus after a flight" outfit of the four, and it's still more considered than most people's game day fit.

Toyota Center, road trip formula: checkerboard denim, an LV belt buckle, and the one bucket hat in the rotation.

Different arena, different jersey coming this fall, same walk. That's really the whole story here: James changed teams four times in his career and the one thing that's followed him to every single one is that he still shows up to work dressed like it matters.
